maya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — couple q's about autoscaler region prioritization and T4 burst strategy. TL;DR: can we get the concrete fallback order and an expected latency hit for cross-region fallthroughs?
chris: Short answer: prefer same-region Dedicated -> same-region Hosted pool -> nearest-region Dedicated -> nearest-region Hosted -> spill to preemptible/spot. Typical latency delta: +20-80ms for nearby region, up to +200-300ms for farther regions or inter-continent. We'll publish a matrix with percentiles.
sylvie: We're assembling that matrix now. Current autoscaler weights (rough): region:100, same-cloud-different-az:85, nearest-region:60, preemptible/spot:30. Those map to rank order in the routing layer.
ops-bot: autoscaler-service: deployed autoscaler-policy-v1.14 to canary at 15:03 UTC — monitor rollout.
dustin: Couple of operational Qs: 1) When does the T4 burst pool get prewarmed versus cold-started? 2) Is customer traffic automatically promoted to prewarm buckets or does it require reserved buckets?
chris: Burst pool prewarm triggers when forecasted demand crosses the 10m sustained threshold (we use short-term forecasts + spike detectors). Promotion: for Hosted burst we try to prewarm automatically based on forecast; for Dedicated reserved buckets it's explicit. We're tuning thresholds after yesterday's spike.
zara: Any changes to per-tenant fairness? Yesterday noisy neighbors pushed some small customers into SLO violations.
sylvie: Yes — we've rolled a soft-tenant-cap in the canary. Also testing a 'slowdown' policy that reduces max concurrency for heavy tenants to protect small ones. Example snippet (canary config):
```json
{
  "tenant_weights": {"default": 1, "high": 0.6},
  "max_concurrency_per_tenant": 64,
  "noisy_neighbor_slowdown": {"enabled": true, "threshold_rps": 500}
}
```
chris: Note — slowdown is a gradual throttle, not hard kill. It buys ~30-60s to failover to another pool or for the tenant to shed load.
liam: From a product/comms perspective: we'll add the fallback/latency matrix to the console's infra docs and a short FAQ explaining what customers should expect during fallthroughs. ETA: next week for console doc.
maya: Action items: chris + sylvie to post the detailed policy doc + fallback matrix as a PR to infra-docs by EOD Wednesday; then ops to flip canary and monitor error budgets. Also, create an external FAQ blurb for support to send to affected customers.
chris: Ack — PR by EOD Wed. I'll include the percentile latency table and an example routing diagram.
sylvie: I'll own the canary rollout and make the tenant-weight knob visible in the console canary panel.
dustin: I'll prepare a short runbook for oncall describing the signs to flip to manual failover if prewarm doesn't kick in.
maya: Awesome — thanks everyone :clap:
